broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior Gram-matrix approach includes the two-sphere cubic case algorithmically, so that consequence is not claimed novel. None of these formulations determines in all dimensions the simultaneous three-sector collision or the exact two crossing conditions. The higher-dimensional large-sieve estimate bounds the maximal concentration but does not determine eigenvectors and equality loci. The older general methods make the spectral integrals computable, not the new exact all-dimensional classification automatically stated.

value.rationale: A natural polar-gap observation geometry exhibits two distinct, dimension-explicit optimal-mode changes. The first is a simultaneous three-sector crossing of multiplicity (d−1)(d+2)/2, not found in the simpler quadratic case.
